subject: ThermoCare: private deployment gating & next milestones
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@thermocare.com>, Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@thermocare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ThermoCare: private deployment gating & next milestones

Thanks for the time this morning — quick recap and next steps so everyone's aligned.

Key business/regulatory drivers we captured:
- ThermoCare needs PHI handling that stays in-county (US) for production workloads; EU residency for analytics subset later in 2027.
- Primary motivation is a regulation-driven air-gap option for certain clinical models; procurement requires evidence (SOC2 + network design).

Technical constraints called out during the call:
- Hosting model: customer-managed VPC (private) w/ no inbound SSH or persistent public IPs; egress-only proxies preferred.
- Only TLS 1.2+ outbound allowed; firewall only permits egress to allowlisted IPs/ranges.
- NetSecure will manage perimeter firewall and must provide exact ACLs; ThermoCare's security policy requires a non-routable peering pattern (private peering + NAT for outbound).
- KMS/HSM: must integrate with ThermoCare KMS for model keys; customer expects HSM-backed key wrap for persisted artifacts.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 summary and sample audit logs required for procurement review (see attachment).

Performance/ops notes:
- Latency SLO target: 100ms p50 for inference in steady-state (we discussed dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback).
- Throughput estimate: 75 requests/min initially, burst to 300/min during peak (planning for autoscaling/dedicated pool).

Attachments included: ThermoCare-SOC2-summary.pdf, thermocare-network-sketch.png (network sketch is high level).

Proposed immediate next steps (owners + dates):
1) NetSecure (ops@netsecure.co) to share firewall/ACL template and contact for NetOps — due Tue 6/1. (Tom + Sarah)
2) Redwood to produce an architecture playbook showing peering, egress pattern, and KMS integration options — draft by Mon 5/31. (Jonas)
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive (NetOps + Security + Redwood infra) — propose Wed 6/2 10:00 AM PT; please confirm availability.
4) ThermoCare procurement will validate SOC2 + audit artifacts; if any gaps, list them in the shared drive link. (Sarah)

Open questions we want answered on the next call:
- Can ThermoCare accept a short-lived egress allowlist for Redwood verifier IPs, or do they require a carrier-independent peering model?
- Does ThermoCare require on-prem HSM or will a cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys suffice?

If any of the above is incorrect or missing, call it out and I'll update. Thanks again — I'll push the draft playbook to the Drive folder and update HubSpot.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@thermocare.com>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ThermoCare: private deployment gating & next milestones

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful and accurate. A couple quick clarifications:
- Procurement is expecting SOC2 evidence plus one example month of anonymized audit logs (redacted ok) for the inference control plane; our vendor/security team will confirm exact format.
- NetSecure will be our firewall vendor. I looped Tom (NetSecure contact) above — Tom, can you confirm you can provide the ACL template by 6/1?

Tom: our primary ask is a non-routable peering setup with egress-only NAT and allow-listing for Redwood IPs; we will not permit inbound peering. Also, for KMS, at minimum we need KMS key wrapping that can be audited; I will confirm whether that must be on-prem HSM vs cloud HSM. Procurement target: sign SOW by end of June, so timing is a bit tight.

I'll confirm availability for Wed 6/2 for the NetOps call.

Best,
Sarah
VP Product & Security Operations | ThermoCare
sarah.lin@thermocare.com | +1 (617) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: ThermoCare constraints — notes

Internal quick note before the NetOps call.

1) HSM path: if ThermoCare insists on on-prem HSM for key wrapping, we'll need to scope a connector and potentially a small private appliance or bring-your-own-key pattern. That will add procurement complexity and may push timeline by ~3–4 weeks.

2) Networking: egress-only with allowlist is straightforward for hosted egress endpoints, but if they refuse any public egress we'll need to plan a private peering + proxy in their VPC. That increases operational overhead and will likely require Dedicated capacity.

3) Commercial ask: procurement timeline end of June means we should propose a short-term dedicated pilot (30–60 days) priced conservatively so they can validate performance and auditing before committing to an annual reserved capacity.

Action: I'll draft two commercial options (pilot & reserved) and share prior to Mon 5/31; plan to review on Mon with Jonas.

—Ben
